rationale: Implementation matches spec intent and is well-tested at the component level, but the acceptance lens found the utils-level test coverage for skillBundleUtils.ts partially unmet: the spec's Testing section explicitly calls for getBundleTotals-level tests crossing the size/count ceilings (under both, exceeding size only, exceeding count only, exceeding both), and the current tests only cover empty/sum/missing-size_bytes at that layer plus a loose regex assertion in the combined-ceiling component test. 2 other minor findings (hardcoded "10 MB" string, unverified truncation-copy claim) and 3 low-priority observations (size_bytes undercount for backend-loaded files, near-threshold display rounding, NaN/negative guard) were triaged as non-blocking: the size_bytes-coalesces-to-0 behavior and the enforcement-copy wording are both explicitly spec-mandated (requirements 2 and 5's example wording), and the rest are cosmetic. All three review lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran successfully with no failures; the spec was present and fully read.

business_review.criterion: 1. Warning appears in SkillBundleFilesSection when bundle exceeds 10MB total size or 100 file count
2. Missing/undefined size_bytes on any file treated as 0 for the size total
3. Warning is non-blocking — never prevents saving the skill
4. Warning names which limit(s) are exceeded with current values (size, count, or both)
5. Test coverage for empty bundle, under both ceilings, exceeding size only, exceeding count only, exceeding both, and missing size_bytes contributing 0
business_review.notes: Covered at the component level (SkillBundleFilesSection.test.tsx) via a loose regex for the combined case; skillBundleUtils.test.ts itself only covers empty/sum/missing-size_bytes and has no dedicated test crossing MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES/MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_FILE_COUNT at the getBundleTotals layer.

business_review.criterion: 6. Uses existing InfoWarning component with WARNING type
7. Constants MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES (10MB) and MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_FILE_COUNT (100) added to src/constants/skills.ts
8. Backend seeding/ledger enforcement explicitly out of scope

standards_review.notes: All 3 commits (5246cfdeb, 85e38e0aa, b10e1bfe3) use the EPMCDME-15558: <summary> format consistent with recent repo history.
Diff touches no dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink, redirect, cross-window message, or secret/config value — guide's checklist is not applicable to this change.

findings.problem: skillBundleUtils.test.ts lacks tests at the getBundleTotals layer that exercise the actual MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES/MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_FILE_COUNT ceilings (under both, exceeding size only, exceeding count only, exceeding both), and the combined-warning assertion in SkillBundleFilesSection.test.tsx uses a loose `.*` regex for the MB value instead of pinning the exact expected value as the size-only test does.
findings.impact: If MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES or MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_FILE_COUNT changes, or if getBundleTotals' ceiling-crossing arithmetic regresses, no utils-level test would catch it — the spec's own Testing section calls for this coverage shape explicitly, and the loose regex means a wrong-but-plausible MB string in the combined case would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add getBundleTotals-focused tests in skillBundleUtils.test.ts for: under both ceilings, exceeding size only, exceeding count only, and exceeding both (asserting against MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES/MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_FILE_COUNT directly). Tighten the combined-warning test's regex to pin the exact expected MB value.

deferred_notes: 2 findings deferred as non-blocking: (1) blind+acceptance lenses both flagged the literal "10 MB" string appearing 3 times in SkillBundleFilesSection.tsx's warning messages instead of being derived from MAX_SKILL_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES/formatFileSize — a real but cosmetic drift risk if the constant ever changes; (2) blind lens flagged that the warning copy's "Only files up to these limits will be copied into a new workspace" phrasing describes truncation/enforcement behavior not implemented in this diff — this matches the spec's own example wording and the explicitly out-of-scope backend seeding/ledger work, so it is intentional, pre-approved copy, not a defect. 3 additional low-priority observations dismissed as noise: size_bytes coalescing to 0 for backend-loaded files without populated metadata (spec requirement #2 mandates this exact behavior), formatFileSize's toFixed(1) rounding near the threshold (e.g. displaying "10.0 MB" for a value just over 10MB), and the absence of a NaN/negative-value guard in getBundleTotals (input is trusted File.size via fileToSkillCompanionFile).
lens_coverage: blind: ran, no failures. edge-case: ran, no failures. acceptance: ran against the full text of spec.md, no failures. No oversized-diff degradation (diff was 252 lines across 5 files).
